text:
sophie: Thinking about a follow-up to the pin/lease RFC — proposal to introduce a sparse-lease mode to reduce metadata size for large multi-tenant rollouts. idea: leases become lightweight pointers (opaque id + minimal TTL + optional affinity tag) instead of carrying full model refs. tradeoffs below. @rahul @jamie PTAL

rahul: Thinking out loud — this could save egress/storage on heavy tenants. Q: how do clients fallback if a lease id is unknown?

sophie: fallback plan: servers will accept both old `pin` objects and new `lease` tokens. clients should treat unknown lease ids as "soft-miss" and call the resolution endpoint to get full model ref. server returns 200 + `resolution_hint` when available, 404 if truly unknown.

jamie: Sounds fine but need a compatibility timeline. We can't force clients to resolve synchronously in hot paths. Suggest 3-phase rollout: 1) accept+emit telemetry, 2) server-side resolution cache + background backfill, 3) deprecate embedded pins after 6 months.

rahul: For phase 2, we should expose a non-blocking SDK helper `resolveLease(lease_id)` that can run in background and populate local cache. If it fails, app uses primary model fallback. Keep latency SLOs intact.

sophie: Agreed. Also propose an explicit `lease_kind` enum: `full`, `sparse`, `ephemeral`. `full` = existing pinned model object; `sparse` = pointer-only; `ephemeral` = single-use transient leases used for canaries. Example payload we discussed:
```json
{
  "lease_kind": "sparse",
  "lease_id": "sha256:2f3b...",
  "ttl_seconds": 7200,
  "affinity": "region:us-west-2",
  "hints": {"version_stability": "stable"} // optional, small
}
```

tess: Two important telemetry asks: mark requests that hit a `sparse` lease resolution path (so we can measure resolution miss %), and emit resolution latency histogram. We'll need a dashboard. Also add a counter for leases that resolve to different model refs over time (regressions).

jamie: On the server side, we should keep a temporary resolution cache with LRU + TTL tuned to workload, and a fallback queue to fetch missing pins lazily. Also need a migration job to convert heavy tenants to `sparse` mode to avoid sudden storage churn.

rahul: Security note — lease_id should be non-guessable and HMAC-signed so clients can't spoof affinity. If `affinity` carries tenant info, make sure we strip tenant IDs from telemetry or hash them.

sophie: Good call. We'll use `lease_id = hmac(kms_key, model_ref|epoch|rand)` and include `sig` if needed. Also add `compat_version` integer so we can evolve the token format without breaking older resolvers.

jamie: API schema compatibility: servers accept both `{ pin: {...} }` and `{ lease: {...} }`. For new writes we default to `lease` when tenant opts-in. Keep read path tolerant. We'll add a feature flag `use_sparse_lease` per tenant.

tess: For rollout, do a canary where 1% of requests return `lease_kind=sparse` for a select internal tenant, monitor miss rate and resolution latency for 48h. If miss_rate > 1% or resolution p95 > 200ms, rollback.

rahul: Clients: docs + SDK release required. We'll provide an adapter that maps old `pin` fields to a resolved model ref automatically. Call out failure modes in the changelog: treat unresolved lease as transient and retry resolution with exponential backoff.

sophie: Edgecases: what if a lease resolves to a different model ref mid-session? Propose `session_stickiness` header: server can attach `resolved_at` and `resolved_model_id` when returning a resolution so clients can decide whether to keep the prior model for session continuity.

jamie: Add a server-side policy for "sticky for X minutes" based on the lease TTL; default stickiness = min(lease_ttl, 300s). Make it configurable per tenant.

tess: Minor: add a telemetry tag `lease_migration` with values `created`, `resolved`, `evicted`, `expired`, `renewed`. That will make dashboards easier.

ops-bot: deploybot: Canary rollout created for tenant `internal-canary-3` with feature flag `use_sparse_lease=true` at 2026-03-23T15:12:00Z :rocket:

rahul: Thanks, @ops-bot. Next steps: I can draft the SDK adapter PR (non-breaking), @sophie can draft the server resolver + cache design doc, @tess will define telemetry metrics and dashboard spec. Then we'll schedule the 1% canary next week.

sophie: I'll open the design doc today and include the HMAC format, compat_version migration plan, and the three-phase rollout checklist. Anything else?

jamie: Also add a short ops playbook for `resolution flood` (if resolution endpoint is overloaded) — e.g., auto-scale, circuit-break to full pins, and alert.

sophie: noted. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
